notes: All 21 HVS-numbered objects from the 42-star Hypervelocity Star Survey sample are included as follow_up: T:p2-b4 says the paper studies the 42 earlier-survey radial-velocity outliers, T:p1-b12 records that 21 stars were already significantly unbound in radial velocity alone, and T:p2-b10 defines HVS numbers as the unbound objects. The 19 HVS objects with Gaia data have positive v_rf-v_esc in Table 2 (I:p10-b0); HVS15 and HVS24 are marginal but remain HVS candidates. HVS14 and HVS23 are among the 42-star sample but lack Gaia data and were dropped from further consideration (T:p2-b12); they are retained here as identifiable prior unbound candidates. B-prefixed objects are the paper's bound sample; B537 and B598 have Galactic-center-like trajectories but are explicitly bound (T:p7-b5), so they are not counted. The text names only HVS1, HVS4, HVS5, and HVS6 individually among the seven probable Galactic-center HVS; that unenumerated subset is not used to limit the roster. No Gaia source IDs are supplied in the paper.

HVS1: Table 2 lists v_rf = 669.8 ± 6.6 km/s for HVS1, but v_rf is explicitly defined as the heliocentric radial velocity transformed to the Galactic frame (Eq. 1, Section 2.1), i.e. a rest-frame velocity, so it is not entered under radial_velocity per the rules. Table 2's p_GC HVS (0.41959) and p_Disk Runaway (0.13256) are probabilities of origin, not bound/unbound probabilities, so they are not entered. HVS1's adopted proper motion is the HST value (Section 2.2.2, T:p4-b4); the Gaia DR2 values are also reported in Table 1. GPS1 has no measurement for HVS1. The 100 kpc distance comes from the Introduction's description of the Brown et al. (2005) discovery, not from a per-star table.

HVS4: Table 1 (T:p3-b0) gives three proper-motion sets for HVS4; the text (T:p4-b4) states HVS4 is one of three stars for which a weighted mean of Gaia and HST is adopted, but no numeric weighted mean is reported, so only the published source values are recorded. Table 2 (T:p10-b0) gives v_rf = 551.7 ± 7.3 km/s; this is a heliocentric radial velocity transformed to the Galactic frame, not a heliocentric/barycentric radial velocity, so it is omitted under the radial_velocity definition. Table 2's p_GC HVS and p_Disk Runaway are origin probabilities, not bound/unbound probabilities. No individual heliocentric distance or parallax is reported for HVS4.

HVS5: HVS5 is listed in Tables 1 and 2. Table 2's v_rf is the Galactic-frame line-of-sight velocity, not heliocentric/barycentric, and it is not the total 3D Galactic rest-frame speed; it is therefore not entered as radial_velocity or galactic_rest_frame_velocity. The paper gives no individual HVS5 parallax or heliocentric distance; Table 2 R is recorded as galactocentric_radius. Table 2 p_GC HVS and p_Disk Runaway are origin likelihoods, not bound/unbound probabilities. The adopted HVS5 proper motion is Gaia; HST and GPS1 values are retained as reported comparison measurements.

HVS6: The reported v_rf = 501.1 ± 6.3 km/s is a heliocentric radial velocity transformed to the Galactic frame (Table 2), so it is not recorded as radial_velocity under the rules; no heliocentric/barycentric radial velocity, total Galactic rest-frame speed, heliocentric distance, individual parallax, or bound probability is reported for HVS6. The text states that HVS6 is one of the 18<g<19 stars for which a weighted mean Gaia/HST proper motion is adopted, although Table 1 lists g=19.06; the adopted weighted mean is not tabulated numerically. (T:p4-b4, T:p3-b0)

HVS7: T:p10-b0 reports v_rf = 397.7 ± 6.8 km/s for HVS7, but T:p2-b4 explicitly defines v_rf as the heliocentric radial velocity transformed to the Galactic frame; it is therefore not included as radial_velocity under the supplied definition. The Table 2 entries p_GC HVS and p_Disk Runaway are origin probabilities, not bound/unbound probabilities. T:p4-b4 indicates the paper adopts Gaia proper motions for bright g<18 stars with σ_HST > 2σ_Gaia, which applies to HVS7.

HVS8: For HVS8, Table 1 (T:p3-b0; I:p3-b0) reports three separate proper-motion measurements (Gaia DR2, HST, and GPS1), all retained; the text does not explicitly state a single adopted proper motion for HVS8. The paper also notes that for HVS8 it adds ±0.5 mas/yr in quadrature to the published HST proper-motion error (T:p3-b7), but Table 1 values are recorded as listed. Table 2 R = 58.3 ± 10.8 kpc is explicitly the Galactocentric radial distance, not a heliocentric distance, so it is recorded as galactocentric_radius; no individual heliocentric distance or parallax for HVS8 is supplied. Table 2 v_rf (T:p10-b0; I:p10-b0) is a heliocentric radial velocity transformed to the Galactic frame, not a heliocentric/barycentric line-of-sight velocity, so it is not recorded as radial_velocity. Table 2 p_GC HVS and p_Disk Runaway are probabilities of origin, not bound/unbound probabilities, so they are not recorded.

HVS9: For HVS9, Table 2 reports v_rf = 458.8 ± 6.1 km/s (T:p10-b0), but the paper defines v_rf as the heliocentric radial velocity transformed to the Galactic frame (T:p2-b4); because this is a Galactic-rest-frame line-of-sight velocity, it is not recorded as radial_velocity under the stated exclusion. No heliocentric/barycentric radial velocity, total Galactic rest-frame speed, or bound/unbound probability is reported for HVS9. The paper states that HVS9 is one of three stars for which a weighted mean of Gaia and HST proper motion is adopted, but does not report the numeric weighted mean (T:p4-b4).

HVS10: HVS10 is listed in Table 1 (T:p3-b0) and Table 2 (T:p10-b0). The paper adopts the HST proper motion for HVS10 (T:p4-b4). I did not extract the Table 2 v_rf value as radial_velocity: the paper defines v_rf as the heliocentric radial velocity transformed to the Galactic frame, not as a heliocentric/barycentric line-of-sight radial velocity. The Table 2 p_GC HVS and p_Disk Runaway values are probabilities of origin, not bound/unbound probabilities. No individual heliocentric distance, parallax, total Galactic rest-frame speed, or bound/unbound probability is reported for HVS10 in the supplied material. The Table 2 R value is a Galactocentric radial distance, not a heliocentric distance.

HVS12: Table 2 gives v_rf = 417.4 ± 8.1 km s^-1 for HVS12 (T:p10-b0). This is the heliocentric radial velocity transformed to the Galactic frame via Equation 1, so it is not recorded as radial_velocity under the rule excluding velocities relative to the local/Galactic standard of rest. No individual heliocentric radial velocity, distance, or parallax is tabulated for HVS12. For HVS12 the paper adopts the HST proper motion (Section 2.2.2, T:p4-b4) rather than the Gaia or GPS1 values. Table 2's p_GC HVS and p_Disk Runaway are origin probabilities, not bound/unbound probabilities, and are not recorded.

HVS13: HVS13 is listed in Table 1 (T:p3-b0) and Table 2 (T:p10-b0). Table 1's GPS1 proper motions are absent for HVS13 (shown as ···), so only Gaia and HST proper motions are extracted. The text at T:p4-b4 explicitly adopts HST proper motions for HVS13. Table 2 reports v_rf = 418.5 ± 10.8 km/s, v_rf − v_esc = 170 km/s, p_GC HVS = 0.12816, and p_Disk Runaway = 0.84341, but v_rf is a heliocentric radial velocity transformed to the Galactic frame rather than a heliocentric/barycentric line-of-sight radial velocity, and the probabilities are origin probabilities rather than bound/unbound probabilities; these are therefore not mapped to radial_velocity or bound_probability/unbound_probability. Table 2's R is Galactocentric radial distance, not heliocentric distance; no individual heliocentric distance or parallax for HVS13 is reported.

HVS14: HVS14 is not listed in Table 1 (which contains the 39 stars with usable Gaia proper motions), nor does it appear in Table 2 or Figure 2. Section 2.2 states: "The three missing stars (HVS14, HVS23, and B149) have too few Gaia measurements for a robust solution. We drop them from further consideration."
